normalized.title: NAVISP EL1-132 DEVELOPMENT AND VALIDATION OF FLEXIBLE ELORAN/GNSS SIGNAL SIMULATOR- EXPRO+
normalized.description: The increasing dependence on GNSS for positioning, navigation and timing (PNT) services has highlighted vulnerabilities to jamming,spoofing, interference and space-weather effects. eLORAN is emerging as a resilient terrestrial complement to GNSS, but its adoptionrequires advanced tools capable of realistically testing and validating hybrid GNSS/eLORAN solutions. This activity will develop and validate a flexible, modular and future-proof eLORAN/GNSS signal simulator, synchronised with commercial GNSS simulators and supported by dedicated Receiver Analysis and Validation Tools. The simulator will provide high-fidelity signal generation, propagation modelling, multi-chain and multi-time-reference capabilities, and record-and-replay functions, enabling realistic end-to-end validation of resilient PNT solutions across timing, maritime and other application domains.

originalText: {"job":"institution-ESA-issued-competition","collectionState":"reconciled","verifiedOpen":false,"spaceRelevance":"not_assessed","recordType":"discovery_candidate","evidence":{"file":"institution-ESA-issued-competition/page-1-48afbe9a395a9d9c0c916a959d43b0c8cf010624de16cc6fbf8e5497f62b1252.json","sha256":"48afbe9a395a9d9c0c916a959d43b0c8cf010624de16cc6fbf8e5497f62b1252","row":7,"retrievedAt":"2026-11-11T10:28:59.747Z"},"original":{"activityNumber":"1000047218","closingDate":"2026-11-16T13:00:00","clarificationRequestDeadline":"2026-11-09T13:00:00","description":"The ESA Antenna Laboratory operates several unique antenna and RF material measurement facilities, including the Sub-mmWave Scanner(SMS), LORENTZ cryogenic near-field scanner, and CATR Material Characterisation Facility. These facilities support antenna and RF characterisation activities covering a frequency range extending from microwave to sub-millimetre-wave frequencies and are routinely used in support of ESA programmes, technology developments, industrial activities and research campaigns.Operation ofthese facilities relies on dedicated custom-developed software that interfaces with motion control systems, network analysers and auxiliary equipment to perform automated measurements, collect measurement data and generate outputs suitable for post-processing andanalysis. Overthe past decade, this software has evolved through multiple development and maintenance activities, supporting successive laboratory upgrades and increasingly demanding measurement campaigns. The software currently comprises three principal application domains:            SMS scanner control software.            LORENTZ scanner control software.            CATR Material Characterisation control software.In addition, a growing set of shared software components has been introduced to provide common functionality across facilities, including hardware abstraction, configuration management, measurement orchestration, data management and graphical user interfaces. Historically, software development activities were executed through a number of independent projects. Consequently, different facilities evolved at different rates and software versions diverged over time. Recent maintenance activities have established a common software management approach based on GitLab repositories, issue tracking mechanisms and shared software components, improving traceability and maintainability of the software assets. The LORENTZ and CATR applications now share a modern architecture built around common software libraries and hardware abstraction layers. The SMS software remains operational but is based on anearlier architecture and represents the principal remaining source of technical debt within the software suite. Long-term sustainability of the Antenna Laboratory software therefore requires continued maintenance, harmonisation and progressive migration towards acommon software framework.The software environment further depends on several third-party components, including software drivers and interfaces fromKeysight, ACS Motion Control, Trio Motion Technology and other equipment suppliers. normalized.title: SOFTWARE UPDATES SMS, MATERIAL AND LORENTZ - EXPRO+
normalized.description: The ESA Antenna Laboratory operates several unique antenna and RF material measurement facilities, including the Sub-mmWave Scanner(SMS), LORENTZ cryogenic near-field scanner, and CATR Material Characterisation Facility. These facilities support antenna and RF characterisation activities covering a frequency range extending from microwave to sub-millimetre-wave frequencies and are routinely used in support of ESA programmes, technology developments, industrial activities and research campaigns.Operation ofthese facilities relies on dedicated custom-developed software that interfaces with motion control systems, network analysers and auxiliary equipment to perform automated measurements, collect measurement data and generate outputs suitable for post-processing andanalysis. Overthe past decade, this software has evolved through multiple development and maintenance activities, supporting successive laboratory upgrades and increasingly demanding measurement campaigns. The software currently comprises three principal application domains:            SMS scanner control software.            LORENTZ scanner control software.            CATR Material Characterisation control software.In addition, a growing set of shared software components has been introduced to provide common functionality across facilities, including hardware abstraction, configuration management, measurement orchestration, data management and graphical user interfaces. Historically, software development activities were executed through a number of independent projects. Consequently, different facilities evolved at different rates and software versions diverged over time. Recent maintenance activities have established a common software management approach based on GitLab repositories, issue tracking mechanisms and shared software components, improving traceability and maintainability of the software assets. The LORENTZ and CATR applications now share a modern architecture built around common software libraries and hardware abstraction layers. The SMS software remains operational but is based on anearlier architecture and represents the principal remaining source of technical debt within the software suite. Long-term sustainability of the Antenna Laboratory software therefore requires continued maintenance, harmonisation and progressive migration towards acommon software framework.The software environment further depends on several third-party components, including software drivers and interfaces fromKeysight, ACS Motion Control, Trio Motion Technology and other equipment suppliers. Maintaining compatibility withcommercial operating systems, hardware drivers and measurement instruments is therefore an essential part of maintaining the operational capability of the Antenna Laboratory. normalized.description: Nitrous oxide (N2O) is an important greenhouse gas that also contributes to stratospheric ozone depletion. However, it requires data converters and RF front-ends for each antenna element, increasing the complexity and power consumption.In this activity, a digital beamforming IP core will be developed, fabricated as a scaled Engineering Model test chip and tested based on ultra sub-micron technology (targeting 7nm or lower). Power consumption shall be minimised, targeting 300mW per channel. Selectable waveform specific features shall be implemented to support a wide range of use casesincluding pre-coding and beam hopping. The IP core shall enable Beamforming Networks with a total bandwidth scalable from GHz to hundreds of GHz for dynamic beam configuration, to achieve a BFIC of 32 GHz capacity with scalable frequency from L-Band to Ka-Band and frequency agnostic topology.This activity will be implemented in a phased approach where:- Phase 1 includes a comparative architectural study of at least four digital beam forming IC integration models. An evaluation of technology node implications shall be performed (e.g. leading-edge vs. trailing-edge). Phase 1 shall explore if a common architecture could support different use-cases (broadband, D2D) e.g. lowering DAC/ADC sampling rates and smart switching (bypassing digital mixing, decimation/interpolation) to maintain beam count while adjusting per-beam bandwidth. A system topology shall be evaluated and defined from the digital processor to the antenna for the placement of the beamforming network (daisy chain, star etc.). The output of Phase 1 is an evaluation of the critical IP blocks via design simulation concluding with tape-out of the design. Phase 1 budget is up to 1,200kEur.- In Phase 2 the architecture and technology for the beamforming chip IP shall be fully designed, implemented and tested to scaled engineering model level. This test chip will be representative of a scaled version of the final potential product. Scaled EM testing will include radiation exposure, thermal cycling, and performance benchmarking against existing space-grade beamforming chips.IP cores developed in this activity shall be available for further development by ESA Member State and Canadian industries at fair and reasonable market conditions.

normalized.description: Development of a compact optical atomic clock module (physics package) for PNT applications. normalized.title: EO4SLOVENIA - AN EO BASED SOLUTION FOR NATURAL HAZARDS AND WATER RESOURCES IN SLOVENIA - EXPRO+
normalized.description: Water Resources Management (WRM) and Disaster Risk Management (DRM) are two thematic areas that are important in Slovenia. In 2025 a preparatory activity concerning the contribution of satellite data for different thematic areas has highlighted the needs of priorities of a group of nationally mandated stakeholders from both the WRM sector and the DRM sector. While the ESA Digital Twin Earth (ESA DTE) programme is looking at integrating Earth Observation (EO) satellite capabilities in future operational Digital Twins ecosystems, including the potential future evolution of DestinE and other operational DT initiatives in Europe, this activity is a precursor development under the FutureEO programme to prepare the ground for an EO based digital ecosystem and connect EO data, processingchains and modelling. This FutureEO activity aims to implement and demonstrate a preliminary Digital Twin Precursor to prefigure potential EO based Digital Twin developments. This ITT refers to implementing an EO-based Digital Twin precursor for the themes Water Resources Management and Disaster Risk Management for Slovenia identified through community consultation and considered to be mature enough to start a large activity. For both WRM and DRM themes, the project shall deliver end-to-end pre-operational solutions, fullyimplemented, conceptually and technically mature, scientifically validated, and fully tested by a representative set of early adopters.

normalized.title: M-IND - INDUSTRIALISATION OF MID-SIZE PLATFORMS FOR LEO CONSTELLATIONS (SAR OPTICAL)
normalized.description: Multiple studies on "Industrialisation of mid-size platforms for LEO constellations in Earth Observation".  This activity is part of the "vertical axis" of the M-IND (Mid-size satellite INDustrialisation) initiative and it is intended for mid-size satellite integrators in order to support the scaling-up of the production of European mid-size satellite (100-500 kg) for Earth Observation applications with LEO constellations. The envisaged solutions and roadmaps shall enable cost-efficient, resilient and high-rate manufacturing aligned with future institutional and commercial mission needs in the EarthObservation domain.

normalized.title: NAVISP EL1-134 ALL-WEATHER LASER TIMING AND RANGING LINKS FOR OPTICAL PNT SYSTEMS - EXPRO+
normalized.description: EL1-134 - This activity will investigate innovative techniques to enable continuous optical timing and ranging links under all weather conditions, addressing a key challenge for operational optical PNT (Positioning, Navigation, and Timing) systems. Optical satellite-to-ground links, such as those planned for ESA's OpSTAR mission, are vulnerable to atmospheric effects, particularly cloud cover, which can degrade or completely interrupt communications with an Optical Ground Station (OGS). The study will assess and experimentally demonstrate atmospheric transmission enhancement techniques designed to improve link availability under adverse weather conditions. It will evaluate whether these approaches can maintain accurate and reliable timing and ranging measurements between laser terminals representative of future operational optical PNT systems.
